Low-level Functions to generate draws from the posterior distribution of model coefficients

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/samplers.R
post_draws.Rd

Low-level Functions to generate draws from the posterior distribution of model coefficients

Generate posterior draws from a fitted model

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
generate_draws(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
post_draws(model, ...)

post_draws(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
post_draws(
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  index = NULL,
  parametrized = TRUE
)

generate_draws(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
generate_draws(
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  index = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
generate_draws(model, ...)

Arguments

model

a fitted model from mgcv::gam(), mgcv::bam(), scam::scam(), or gamm4::gamm4(), or a model inheriting from these classes. See gamm4_support for sampling from gamm4 fits.

...

arguments passed to methods.

n_draws

positive integer; total retained draws across all chains. Required when generating draws. With method = "user", the supplied matrix determines the count; an explicit count must agree with its rows.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

seed

numeric or NULL; seed for the complete sampling operation. An explicit seed restores the caller's random-number state on exit.

method

character; which algorithm to use to sample from the posterior. Currently implemented methods are: "gaussian" and "mh". "gaussian" calls gaussian_draws() which uses a Gaussian approximation to the posterior distribution. "mh" uses a simple Metropolis Hastings sampler which alternates static proposals based on a Gaussian approximation to the posterior, with random walk proposals. Note, setting t_df to a low value will result in heavier-tailed statistic proposals. See mgcv::gam.mh() for more details.

n_cores

positive integer; maximum concurrent MH chains using mirai, capped at chains. Existing workers are reused; otherwise temporary workers are created and cleaned up. Only used by method = "mh".

n_threads

positive integer; threads within Gaussian sampling using mvnfast. Defaults to one. This is separate from concurrent MH chains.

burnin

numeric; the length of any initial burn in period to discard. See mgcv::gam.mh().

thin

positive integer; retain every thin iterations after burn-in.

t_df

numeric; degrees of freedom for static multivariate t proposal. See mgcv::gam.mh().

rw_scale

numeric; factor by which to scale posterior covariance matrix when generating random walk proposals. See mgcv::gam.mh().

frequentist

logical; if TRUE, the frequentist covariance matrix of the parameter estimates is used. If FALSE, the Bayesian posterior covariance matrix of the parameters is used. See mgcv::vcov.gam().

unconditional

logical; if TRUE the Bayesian smoothing parameter uncertainty corrected covariance matrix is used, if available for model. See mgcv::vcov.gam(). SCAM models do not support this correction; use unconditional = FALSE.

draws

matrix; user supplied posterior draws to be used when method = "user".

diagnostics

logical; calculate coefficient R-hat, effective sample sizes, and Monte Carlo standard errors using the optional posterior package.

mh_backend

character; "mgcv" preserves mgcv::gam.mh(). "gratia" uses compiled common-family likelihoods. "family" uses a compiled MH loop with callbacks to the fitted family object. Both support independent-observation bam fits. Smoothing parameters and parameters outside the fitted coefficient vector remain fixed. LSS scale and shape coefficients are sampled jointly with location. The family backend caches a full design matrix, smoothing penalty, and proposal factorisation once for all chains.

mvn_method

character; one of "mvnfast" or "mgcv". The default is uses mvnfast::rmvn(), which can be considerably faster at generate large numbers of MVN random values than mgcv::rmvn(), but which might not work for some marginal fits, such as those where the covariance matrix is close to singular.

block_size

positive integer; maximum observation rows per block in the gratia MH evaluator. Large designs are evaluated without storing a full matrix.

dense_limit

numeric; maximum number of design-matrix elements to cache for the gratia MH backend. Use zero to force blockwise evaluation.

index

numeric; vector of indices of coefficients to use. Can be used to subset the mean vector and covariance matrix extracted from model.

parametrized

logical; for SCAM fits, transform Gaussian draws from the unrestricted fitting coefficients using the fitted positivity transform. This preserves the smooth's constraints. With FALSE, return Gaussian draws in the unrestricted fitting coordinates. Only for scam::scam() fits.

Details

Sampling controls must be named. Removed arguments produce migration errors; see vignette("sampling-migration"). Explicit controls that the selected method cannot use are rejected.

For SCAM models, Gaussian draws approximate the distribution of the unrestricted fitting coefficients using Vp (or Ve with frequentist = TRUE), then apply scam's fitted exponential or notExp transformation. This is an approximation in fitting coordinates, rather than an exact constrained posterior. Supplied draws must already use the transformed coordinates in coef(model) order. Numerically singular covariance matrices are sampled by eigen decomposition; negative eigenvalues within 100 * .Machine$double.eps * ncol(V) times the largest absolute eigenvalue are treated as zero. Larger negatives are errors. For weakly identified exponential coefficients, a very large fitting-coordinate variance can yield non-finite transformed draws. Sampling then reports an error because this Gaussian approximation cannot provide usable draws; supply finite transformed draws from a suitable alternative sampler.

For multiple chains, n_draws is the total retained count and must be divisible by chains. Coefficient matrices carry a chain mapping; use as_mcmc_draws() before ordinary matrix operations remove that mapping. Higher-level sampling tables include .chain and .iteration for multiple chains, with .draw unique across chains. Default single-chain table columns are unchanged. Use sampling_diagnostics() to extract coefficient diagnostics before response simulation adds further noise.

The gratia MH backend supports Gaussian identity, Poisson log, binomial logit, Gamma log, and negative binomial log fits. It evaluates the fitted bases at original covariates, including for discrete bam fits. GAMM components, AR1 dependence, paraPen, H, and fits made from pre-fit G objects are unsupported.

The family MH backend calls the fitted family's dev.resids() and linkinv() functions, or ll() for families with multiple linear predictors. This retains response encodings and attributes such as censoring indicators and the mappings between coefficients and predictors. It supports compatible standard, extended, and general mgcv families, including multinomial, Gaussian location-scale, and grouped families. Quasi families, Cox proportional hazards models, GAMM components, AR1 dependence, paraPen, H, and pre-fit G objects are unsupported. The fitted coefficient covariance must be nonsingular. It always caches the full design matrix; block_size and dense_limit apply only to the gratia backend and are rejected for the family backend. The new MH backends reject bam fits with nonzero prescribed smooth contributions: mgcv fitting and prediction can use different offsets for those fits. Supplied coefficient draws can still be evaluated with the native prediction conventions.

All MH backends sample the conditional coefficient posterior with fitted smoothing, dispersion, and additional family parameters fixed. Parameters represented in the fitted coefficient vector are sampled, including scale or covariance coefficients in general families. unconditional applies to Gaussian draws only.

GAM-class fits with linear inequality constraints, including mgcv::scasm() fits, store these as Ain %*% coefficients >= bin. Gaussian sampling uses the fitted covariance matrix without enforcing these inequalities and issues a warning. Sampled smooths can therefore violate the fitted shape constraints. Pointwise intervals computed from the same Gaussian covariance approximation also need not preserve those shapes. All MH backends are unavailable for these fits because the samplers do not enforce their inequalities.

If mgcv::scasm() was fitted with bs > 0, its bs component stores coefficient draws from the native constrained bootstrap in columns. These can be supplied explicitly as draws = t(model$bs) with method = "user". The result then describes bootstrap variation, rather than Gaussian posterior sampling. Gratia does not automatically select these draws. The caller is responsible for the interpretation and constraint feasibility of user-supplied draws.
